lines.text: The family is stable again. Aarav has settled into routine. Neeraj shows him a newspaper article: engineering graduates in their state have an 82% employment rate.
That can't be right. Everyone knows engineers are unemployed.
Rationalization. Aarav has not changed what he wants — he has changed what he believes about the facts.
His desire for a good career is intact. But his map of reality has been quietly redrawn to make the detour feel like the main road.
And if money weren't a problem? If someone paid for everything?
But money is a problem. So why think about it?
And this is state-dependent preference. In his current condition — financial pressure, family obligation — Aarav's desires are chained to what is urgent.
If the condition changed, the preference might change too. When a state persists long enough, the chain becomes invisible.
Nine moments. Nine forces that moved a want. Some preserved Aarav's autonomy. Some eroded it. Some are ambiguous. And all nine produced the same outward result: a man who says he is fine.
